name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd
title: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd - 500312 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: ONGC Q2 FY27 standalone PAT rose over 57% YoY to INR 15,489 crore on crude realisation of USD 92.33/bbl, with record H1 PAT of INR 32,522 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone gross revenue was INR 43,857 crore, up over 33% YoY, helped by improved realisations. Production was broadly flat QoQ but down marginally YoY, hit by DUDP supply-chain delays, offshore weather and an OTPC Tripura offtake shutdown affecting gas. Other expenses rose on a INR 1,861 crore provision for a terminal excise duty receivable under High Court litigation, partly offset by lower OpEx and exchange loss. Management declared a record first interim dividend of INR 8 per share (160%), totalling INR 10,064 crore, and guided FY27 production to about 39 MMT oil equivalent.

financial_highlights.value: INR 8 per share (160%), total outgo INR 10,064 crore

financial_highlights.change: incremental INR 2,859 crore vs APM pricing; over 34% of nomination gas revenue

financial_highlights.value: INR 494 crore loss (Q2); INR 1,100 crore loss (H1)

financial_highlights.change: includes INR 1,861 crore DGFT excise provision, offset by OpEx down INR 609 crore and exchange loss down INR 625 crore

segments.name: Upstream – Western Offshore / Mumbai High
segments.commentary: TSP-I with BP at Mumbai High showing early gains, especially in gas; management cited about 7-8% incremental gas on a daily basis at the uptick start. Fixed fee applies for first two years; performance-linked sharing starts April 2027. TSP for Neelam, Bassein & Satellite awarded in Q2.

segments.name: KG-DWN-98/2 (deepwater)
segments.commentary: Oil output about 19,000 bbl/d. Gas about 2 MMSCMD in Q2, with three wells (about 1.5 MMSCMD) planned for connection in Q4. Subsurface complexity has caused a dip; full peak guided at 3.5 MMSCMD by FY27 end per analyst question.

segments.name: OPaL (petrochemicals)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA INR 147 crore and PAT loss INR 494 crore, as higher feedstock prices from Hormuz disruption offset petchem price rebound. Interest cost was about INR 2,000 crore last year and is expected to fall after INR 18,000 crore equity infusion.

segments.name: International (ONGC Videsh)
segments.commentary: Sakhalin-1 average production 183,000 bbl/d in H1, near pre-2022 levels. Mozambique project about USD 7 billion invested and 49% complete; drawdown expected from next month. Venezuela agreements expected in 3-6 months; no capex figure yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 oil and gas production about 39 MMT oil equivalent.
FY28 production about 0.5 to 1 MMT higher than FY27.
Samudra Manthan: four deepwater exploration wells in FY27 and up to 13 wells in FY28, subject to rig availability (two rigs on hire).
KG-DWN-98/2 gas wells expected to be completed by next quarter; further ramp-up path still under study.
DSF-II volumes expected to start at least towards end of FY27; DUDP about half of wells done.
Capex guided at about USD 3.5-4 billion per year; dividend payout guided around 40%, no change in policy.
capex_capacity: Two Western Offshore development projects awarded in Q2 with combined investment about INR 11,800 crore and 22 MMT oil equivalent potential, completing in 2 to 2.5 years.
Second deepwater rig expected to mobilise this financial year; first rig operational in Mahanadi Basin.
Mozambique LNG: about USD 7 billion invested to date; sovereign guarantee approved; drawdown expected from next month.
Venezuela San Cristobal (sole operator) and Petro Carabobo (joint operator) agreements expected within 3-6 months; no capex disclosed.
Silchar gas discoveries to be monetised via IGGL pipeline expansion.
demand_pricing: Average crude realisation USD 92.33/bbl in Q2 FY27.
Feedstock prices rose due to Hormuz disruption, weighing on OPaL; ethane sourcing from USA via two ships due early 2029 and long-term ethane price talks ongoing.
New petchem marketing company (ONGC Petrochemicals Marketing Ltd) incorporated 7 October 2026 to combine OPaL, ONGC and MRPL marketing; synergies not quantified.
Industry standard field decline cited at 6-8% per year.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of higher other expenses, lower tax rate and higher depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses included INR 1,861 crore provision on DGFT terminal excise duty receivable under High Court litigation; net impact about INR 600 crore after OpEx and exchange loss declines. Lower tax reflected higher non-taxable dividend income (about INR 80 crore benefit). Depreciation included impairment on long-pending exploratory wells.

qa_highlights.question: Production guidance for FY27, FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 about 39 MMT oil equivalent; FY28 about 0.5 to 1 MMT higher. No FY29 figure given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Samudra Manthan wells and benefit quantification?
qa_highlights.answer: Four wells planned this year and up to 13 next year, depending on rigs. Benefit cannot be quantified as it is exploratory.

qa_highlights.question: TSP-I production and KG-DWN-98/2 upside?
qa_highlights.answer: TSP is a field-level 10-year contract; no field-level split given, with details to come from IR. KG-98/2 oil about 19,000 bbl/d; gas wells slipped due to monsoon and cyclone Arnab, now expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: OPaL and petchem marketing synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Synergies not quantifiable yet. OPaL Q2 EBITDA INR 147 crore; H1 INR 90 crore; PAT loss INR 494 crore in Q2 and INR 1,100 crore in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Gas production in KG-98/2 and timing of additional wells?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 gas about 2 MMSCMD; three wells adding about 1.5 MMSCMD planned in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique spend and Venezuela capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 7 billion invested; 49% complete; drawdown next month. Venezuela capex not shared until agreements are signed.

qa_highlights.question: Repatriation of Venezuela and Russia dividends and profits?
qa_highlights.answer: Venezuela dividend (about USD 500 million) still unresolved; new arrangement gives offtake rights. Vankorneft dividend used for Sakhalin abandonment liability. Sakhalin dividend repatriable once declared; no restriction currently.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for excess operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex USD 3.5-4 billion per year; dividend policy unchanged at about 40% payout; diversification opportunities being explored.

qa_highlights.question: TSP baseline decline and Mumbai High production uptick?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give decline rates for TSP, citing long-term measurement; industry decline 6-8% per year cited. Mumbai High gas uptick about 7-8% on incremental daily basis at start.

risks_watch: Production recovery depends on DUDP and KG-98/2 wells being connected next quarter; subsurface complexity may delay ramp-up.
Deepwater rig availability is tight and may limit the 13-well Samudra Manthan plan for FY28.
OPaL remains loss-making due to feedstock costs; ethane sourcing and interest cost reduction need to be seen.
Venezuela dividend receivable and profit repatriation terms remain unresolved.
Litigation on the INR 1,861 crore DGFT excise duty receivable; a court win would reverse the provision.
Hormuz-related supply chain and cost inflation risks to project timelines.
summary.management_tone: Confident on earnings and long-term pipeline, but guarded on specifics: management declined to quantify TSP decline rates, Venezuela capex, petchem synergies and Samudra Manthan benefits, and acknowledged production shortfalls and KG-98/2 subsurface complexity.
key_quotes: Riding on the strong-earning momentum, the company also posted its highest ever H1 profit after tax of INR 32,522 crore.
We are actively addressing these issues, with critical materials now being mobilized and additional wells expected to come on stream in the coming months.
It is a ten -year contract. And as part of contract, we have a plan to achieve a certain upside on that TSP-1.
We are working on that right now. It's definitely a much more complex system than what we had originally envisaged.

adds.what: Second deepwater rig (KG basin) expected to mobilise this financial year
KG-DWN-98/2 three gas wells (~1.5 MMSCMD) for connection in Q4
Two Western Offshore development projects (~INR 11,800 crore, 22 MMT o.e. potential) completing in 2 to 2.5 years
Mozambique LNG (~USD 7 billion invested, 49% complete), drawdown from next month

growth.why: FY27 production guided at about 39 MMT o.e. (held) and FY28 up 0.5-1 MMT, but Q2 production was flat-to-down YoY on offtake and DUDP delays, so growth is only partly backed by specific wells, a second rig and two awarded projects with INR 11,800 crore investment, while the 33% revenue jump came mainly from realisation (USD 92.33/bbl).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 PAT up over 57% YoY to INR 15,489 crore on USD 92.33/bbl realisation, but the INR 1,861 crore DGFT provision and OPaL losses (Q2 PAT loss INR 494 crore on EBITDA of INR 147 crore) cloud the margin path, and OpEx fell INR 609 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three KG-98/2 gas wells (~1.5 MMSCMD) are slated for connection in Q4 and a second deepwater rig is due to mobilise this year, but Q2 production was flat-to-down YoY and the 3.5 MMSCMD peak depends on subsurface work.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 production held at about 39 MMT o.e. and FY28 guided 0.5-1 MMT higher, yet Q2 output was flat QoQ and down marginally YoY on DUDP delays and the OTPC Tripura offtake shutdown.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided at USD 3.5-4 billion a year with two Western Offshore projects (~INR 11,800 crore) awarded in Q2, and Venezuela agreements expected in 3-6 months, but no new capex figure has been disclosed and management deferred some strategic projects.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 at about 39 MMT o.e. and FY28 at +0.5-1 MMT, and cited production shortfalls and KG-98/2 subsurface complexity, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: KG-98/2 gas wells already slipped from the prior quarter on monsoon and cyclone Arnab, and the 3.5 MMSCMD peak still depends on the Q4 connections, while the Samudra Manthan 13-well FY28 plan is capped by rig availability.

rows.label: Mumbai High TSP-I gas uptick
rows.why: Management cited about 7-8% incremental gas on a daily basis at the uptick start, with performance-linked sharing starting April 2027.

rows.label: DGFT excise duty litigation
rows.why: A court win on the INR 1,861 crore terminal excise duty receivable would reverse the provision, but the outcome is not yet known.

rows.label: Venezuela agreements and dividend repatriation
rows.why: San Cristobal and Petro Carabobo agreements are expected in 3-6 months, but the about USD 500 million Venezuela dividend is still unresolved and no capex has been disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on record earnings, dividend and the long-term pipeline, but guarded on TSP decline rates, Venezuela capex, petchem synergies and Samudra Manthan benefits, while analysts pressed on production shortfalls and the KG-98/2 ramp-up.
